Container.Name: zitadel
Container.Overview:
ZITADEL is a self-hosted identity infrastructure platform: SSO (OIDC/SAML), MFA, and user management for your own apps and services.
This template deploys the ZITADEL v4 core/API service only. Since v4, the interactive login pages were split into a separate service (zitadel-login) that MUST be deployed alongside this one, or logging in will fail with a 404 on /ui/v2/login/login. See the companion "zitadel-login" template from the same repository.
Requires an external Postgres 14+ database (not included in this template) and a 32-character Master Key.
IMPORTANT: besides filling in the "Master Key" field below, you MUST also replace the placeholder in "Post Arguments" (under Extra Parameters, near the bottom of the Add Container page) with that exact same key — ZITADEL has a known bug where the environment variable alone isn't reliably read with the start-from-init command, and the container will crash-loop with "no master key provided" if you skip this.
Default admin login after first start: zitadel-admin@zitadel.<your external domain> / Password1! — you will be asked to change this password on first login (unless you disable that below).
Full setup guide: https://github.com/Nebur692/unraid-zitadel-templates
Container.Requires: An external PostgreSQL 14+ database, reachable from this container, plus the companion "zitadel-login" template for the interactive login pages to work.

Config.Name: Master Key
Config.Description: REQUIRED. Exactly 32 characters, used to encrypt secrets at rest. Generate once, keep it safe, never change it after first start (you will lose access to encrypted data). Example: openssl rand -base64 24 | cut -c1-32. IMPORTANT: ZITADEL has a known bug where this environment variable alone is not always read with the start-from-init command — you MUST also replace the placeholder in Post Arguments (Extra Parameters section) with this exact same value, or the container will crash-loop with 'no master key provided'.

Config.Name: External Domain
Config.Description: REQUIRED. The public domain users will use to reach ZITADEL (e.g. sso.example.com), without protocol or port. Must match what your reverse proxy serves.

Config.Name: External Port
Config.Description: The public-facing port your reverse proxy exposes ZITADEL on (usually 443 for HTTPS). This is NOT the container's internal port.

Config.Name: External Secure (HTTPS)
Config.Description: Set to true if users reach ZITADEL over HTTPS (normal case, e.g. behind Nginx Proxy Manager with a valid certificate). Set to false only for plain-HTTP test setups.

Config.Name: TLS Enabled (container-internal)
Config.Description: Whether ZITADEL itself terminates TLS inside the container. Leave false if a reverse proxy (Nginx Proxy Manager, Traefik, Caddy...) handles HTTPS in front of it, which is the recommended setup.

Config.Name: Database Postgres Host
Config.Description: REQUIRED. Hostname or IP of your external Postgres server/container.

Config.Name: Database Postgres Port
Config.Description: Postgres port.

Config.Name: Database Name
Config.Description: Database name ZITADEL will use/create.

Config.Name: Database Admin Username
Config.Description: Username with rights to create the app role/database on first start. IMPORTANT: if your Postgres container was created with a custom POSTGRES_USER (instead of leaving it as the default 'postgres'), that custom user IS your superuser — put that same username here, not 'postgres'. Using the wrong one causes a password authentication failed / restart loop.

Config.Name: Database Admin Password
Config.Description: Password for the admin username above.

Config.Name: Database Admin SSL Mode
Config.Description: SSL mode for the admin connection (disable/require/verify-ca/verify-full).

Config.Name: Database App Username
Config.Description: Username ZITADEL uses day-to-day (created automatically on first start using the admin credentials above, unless it's the same as the admin username).

Config.Name: Database App Password
Config.Description: Password for the day-to-day database user above.

Config.Name: Database App SSL Mode
Config.Description: SSL mode for the app connection (disable/require/verify-ca/verify-full).

Config.Name: Require Password Change On First Login
Config.Description: Whether the default admin account must change its password on first login. Recommended: true. Only has effect on the very first start.

Config.Name: Login Client PAT Path (bootstrap)
Config.Description: CRITICAL, do not change. On first start, ZITADEL writes here the access token that the companion zitadel-login container needs to function. Must point inside the shared bootstrap volume below.

Config.Name: Login Client Machine Username
Config.Description: Do not change unless you know why. Internal service-account username created on first start for the login UI to authenticate as.

Config.Name: Login Client Machine Name
Config.Description: Display name for the internal login-client service account.

Config.Name: Login V2 Required
Config.Description: Do not change: v4 always requires the new login UI. Kept visible for transparency.

Config.Name: Login V2 Base URI
Config.Description: REQUIRED. Full public URL of the login pages, e.g. https://sso.example.com/ui/v2/login/ — must match your External Domain/Port/Secure settings above, with the trailing slash.

Config.Name: OIDC Default Login URL V2
Config.Description: REQUIRED. e.g. https://sso.example.com/ui/v2/login/login?authRequest=

Config.Name: OIDC Default Logout URL V2
Config.Description: REQUIRED. e.g. https://sso.example.com/ui/v2/login/logout?post_logout_redirect=

Config.Name: SAML Default Login URL V2
Config.Description: REQUIRED if you plan to use SAML (e.g. Zabbix). e.g. https://sso.example.com/ui/v2/login/login?samlRequest=

Config.Name: Bootstrap Volume (shared with zitadel-login)
Config.Description: Shared with the zitadel-login container (mounted read-only there) so it can read the login-client.pat token written here on first start. Both templates must point at the exact same host path.

Config.Name: Web UI / API Port
Config.Description: Internal port. Put your reverse proxy in front of this — do not expose it directly to the internet without TLS.
